title: Cloudflare, July 2, 2019: A protection rule brings every server to its knees

subtitle.simple: How one small new rule made websites worldwide unreachable for 27 minutes.
subtitle.tech: WAF rule with catastrophic regex backtracking, rolled out globally, CPU exhaustion, HTTP 502.

headline.simple: Problem: Suddenly millions of websites show only “Error 502”. Why?
headline.tech: Bug: Worldwide CPU exhaustion on all HTTP edges; clients get 502.

text.simple: A visitor opens a website, and the request first goes to Cloudflare's bouncer.
text.tech: The browser sends an HTTPS request to the Cloudflare edge, where the WAF inspects it.

text.simple: The bouncer finds nothing suspicious and fetches the page from the customer's server.
text.tech: No rule matches; the request is forwarded to the origin.

text.simple: The visitor sees the page – this happens many millions of times per second.
text.tech: Response to the client; normal operation at about one third CPU load.

text.simple: An employee releases a small new rule meant to catch a known type of attack.
text.tech: An engineer merges a new XSS rule; the tests check matches but not CPU time.

text.simple: Within seconds the rule goes to every location in the world at once, with no trial run.
text.tech: Quicksilver distributes it globally in seconds, no staged rollout; even in simulate mode it fully runs.

text.simple: For the next visitor, the new rule searches its pattern so clumsily that it tries thousands of paths.
text.tech: The expression .*(?:.*=.*) causes catastrophic backtracking in PCRE: thousands of steps per request.

text.simple: Every new request starts the same guessing, until servers everywhere would need to do more than they can.
text.tech: Every CPU handling HTTP and HTTPS worldwide runs at nearly 100%.

text.simple: The bouncer can't keep up, and visitors of every Cloudflare customer see an error instead of the page.
text.tech: The edges return 502 Bad Gateway for all Cloudflare domains for 27 minutes.

headline.simple: Solution: New rules go to one city first, and the bouncer never tries endlessly again.
headline.tech: Fix: Staged rollout for WAF rules, a regex engine with runtime guarantees, and a CPU limit again.

text.simple: A visitor opens a website, and the request first goes to Cloudflare's bouncer.
text.tech: The browser sends an HTTPS request to the Cloudflare edge, where the WAF inspects it.

text.simple: The bouncer finds nothing suspicious and fetches the page from the customer's server.
text.tech: No rule matches; the request is forwarded to the origin.

text.simple: The visitor sees the page – this happens many millions of times per second.
text.tech: Response to the client; normal operation at about one third CPU load.

text.simple: An employee releases a small new rule meant to catch a known type of attack.
text.tech: An engineer merges a new XSS rule; the test now also measures each rule's CPU time.

text.simple: The rule first goes to a single city, so a mistake can do harm there at most.
text.tech: Staged rollout: first an internal PoP, then canaries, then global, instead of everything in seconds.

text.simple: Also, the bouncer now searches so that it reads each text only once and never tries endlessly.
text.tech: Regex engine with runtime guarantees (RE2 or Rust regex) instead of PCRE, plus a per-rule CPU limit again.

text.simple: Stress test: A visitor makes a request, and even the clumsy rule finishes instantly.
text.tech: The same expression now runs in linear time; CPU stays in the normal range.

text.simple: The bouncer fetches the page from the customer's server as usual.
text.tech: The request is forwarded to the origin as normal.

text.simple: Result: The page loads normally, even though the clumsy rule is active.
text.tech: Result: no CPU bottleneck, no 502, outage risk limited to one stage.
